Editing · Color grading · Before & after · Masking · Presets · Library · Agents & MCP · Performance · Status · Quick start · Roadmap · Downloads · Crafting Apps


## Edit like you mean it LightCraft is a complete darkroom in a single native app. Every adjustment is **non-destructive**, so your originals are never touched. Every slider renders through a **scene-referred, wide-gamut, 32-bit float pipeline**: highlights roll off like film, shadows open up without halos, and colour stays clean from capture to export.
### ☀️ Light **Exposure, Contrast, Highlights, Shadows, Whites, Blacks**, with edge-aware local tone mapping (a guided filter on log-luminance). Pulling −100 Highlights recovers a blown sky without the grey halos you'd get from a naive curve. ### 🎨 Color **White balance** by temperature and tint (Kelvin for raw, relative for JPEG) with presets, Auto and a click-to-neutralise **eyedropper**. **Vibrance** that protects skin tones, **Saturation**, an 8-band **Color Mixer** (hue / saturation / luminance) and 3-way **Color Grading** wheels with blending and balance. All of it is computed in OkLCh, a modern perceptual colour space. ##

basic_info.name: nvidia-macos-driver
basic_info.description: Metal driver for NVIDIA GeForce cards on macOS Sequoia

content.readme:
# NullMoth NVIDIA Driver for macOS

A Metal driver for NVIDIA GeForce cards on macOS 15 Sequoia (Intel Macs and OpenCore PCs). It is open source; the
kernel extensions, the Metal plugin and the shader translator are in this repository. The 1401 app that installs it
(Mac and Windows) is its own project: [1401](https://github.com/nullmoth/1401).

Supported cards are Turing and newer: GTX 16, RTX 20, 30, 40 and 50, TITAN RTX, Quadro RTX and the T-series. Most
testing is done on an RTX 5060, so other cards may have problems that haven't been found yet. See
[card support](docs/CARD-SUPPORT.md) for what has been reported working.

- Changes: [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md), downloads on the [releases page](https://github.com/nullmoth/nvidia-macos-driver/releases)
- Problems: [troubleshooting](docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md), then Send logs from the 1401 app
- Installing macOS from Windows: [1401](https://github.com/nullmoth/1401)
- How it works: [docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md](docs/HOW-IT-WORKS.md)
- Contributing: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md)

If your PC doesn't boot macOS with OpenCore yet, set that up first with the
[OpenCore Install Guide](https://dortania.github.io/OpenCore-Install-Guide/), then install the driver.

Support the work: https://buymeacoffee.com/nullmoth

| | |
|---|---|
| macOS | 15.5 Sequoia or later (tested 15.7.x and 15.8.1), or 26 Tahoe, x86_64 |
| GPUs | NVIDIA Turing and later; developed on an RTX 5060 |
| Metal | Metal 3: argument buffers tier 2, ray tracing, mesh shaders, MPS, MetalFX path |
| Also | OpenGL (through Apple's GL-on-Metal), OpenCL, Core Image, Core ML |

## How it works

```
Metal app ─► NVMTLDriver.bundle ─► translator (Apple AIR → SPIR-V) ─► NVK (Mesa Vulkan + NAK compiler) ─► kexts ─► GPU
```

| Component | Path on disk | Source |
|---|---|---|
| Metal driver plugin | `/Library/GPUBundles/NVMTLDriver.bundle` | `plugin/` |
| Shader translator | inside the plugin (`libnvmtl_translate.dylib`) | `translator/` (LGPL-3.0, based on metal2vulkan) |
| Vulkan back end (NVK) | `/Library/GPUBundles/nvmtl/` | `nvk/nvk-macos.patch` on Mesa `17ca6174` |
| Kernel extensions | `/Library/Extensions/NVRM, NVAccel, NVRMFB, NVRMAGDC` | `kexts/` |
| GPU firmware (GSP) | `/Library/NullMoth/nvfw/nvidia/615.78.08` | NVIDIA, unmodified |

The kernel side runs NVIDIA's own open GPU kernel modules (r610) under macOS. NVRMFB is the display framebuffer,
NVAccel the accelerator WindowServer composites through, NVRMAGDC the display-policy shim.

## Install — by hand

Use the 1401 Mac app below unless you manage your OpenCore config yourself. `install.sh` installs the driver files but
does not change OpenCore, and the driver does not start until OpenCore has these settings:

- `boot-args` include `nvfb=1 nvaccel=1 nvfbheads=4 -nvkmsnosmooth amfi_get_out_of_my_way=0x1 amfi=0x80
  ipc_control_port_options=0`, and not `nv_disable=1` or `-wegnoegpu` (both hide the NVIDIA card)
- `csr-active-config` includes the bits `0x0A43`
- `Misc > Security > SecureBootModel` is `Disabled`
- `Lilu.kext` and `AMFIPass.kext` are in `Kernel > Add` and enabled

Download `nullmoth-nvidia-<version>.tar.gz` from **Releases**, then:

```bash
tar -xzf nullmoth-nvidia-*.tar.gz && cd pkgroot
shasum -a 256 -c SHA256SUMS
sudo ./install.sh
sudo shutdown -r now
```

Every file must say OK in the check. `install.sh` copies the files and rebuilds the Auxiliary Kernel Collection; the
restart is required, because logging out does not load the driver. (Paste the lines without anything after them: the
Terminal on macOS does not treat `#` as a comment, so a pasted comment becomes part of the command.)

macOS asks you to **allow the extensions** in System Settings → Privacy & Security the first time. Allow, then reboot again.

## 1401 Mac app (recommended)

Download the latest `1401-Mac-<version>.dmg` from **Releases**, open it, and run **1401** (the driver package is inside the disk
image, so nothing else to download). Follow its steps. A supported setup must use a verified or explicitly selected OpenCore partition. The app finds the OpenCore that started your Mac (in `EFI/OC` or `EFI/BOOT`, on an
EFI or FAT32 partition), shows every change before making it, backs the config up, installs the driver, and adds
**1401: Remove NVIDIA driver** to the OpenCore boot picker. Choosing that entry removes the driver at the next start and

basic_info.name: disktree
basic_info.description: A treemap for finding and removing what fills your disk, for Omarchy. Rust + GPUI.

content.readme:
# disktree

![disktree: a home directory as a treemap, coloured by kind of data, with reclaimable space hatched and the selection, findings and free space in the side panel](assets/screenshot.png)

Find what is filling a disk, mark what should go, and remove it — with the
volume's free space in view the whole time.

disktree is a treemap for Omarchy. It scans your home directory by default,
draws every directory as a nested mosaic sized by what it really costs on disk,
and lets you walk into it with the keyboard or the mouse. Mark as much as you
like; nothing happens until you review the list and commit, and the permanent
path always asks first.

Built with [GPUI](https://gpui-kit.com/) through
[gpui-omarchy](https://github.com/huacnlee/gpui-omarchy), so it follows your
Omarchy theme and behaves like the rest of the desktop.

## Install

Download `disktree-*-x86_64-linux.tar.gz` (`aarch64-linux` on ARM) from the
[latest release](https://github.com/tobi/disktree/releases/latest), unpack
it, and run `./install.sh` inside (or just copy `disktree` onto your
`PATH`). Or build it:

```sh
git clone https://github.com/tobi/disktree
cd disktree
make install
```

`make install` builds a release binary and puts three things under `~/.local`
(no root needed):

- `~/.local/bin/disktree`
- a desktop entry, so disktree is in the launcher and in a file manager's
  **Open with** for a directory (it adds a handler; it never becomes the
  default)
- an icon

`sudo make install PREFIX=/usr/local` installs system-wide; `make uninstall`
removes exactly what was installed.

On Arch, including Omarchy, disktree is in the AUR:
[`disktree`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/disktree) builds each release
from source, and
[`disktree-bin`](https://aur.archlinux.org/packages/disktree-bin) installs
the release binary:

```sh
yay -S disktree-bin
```

You need Rust 1.97 or newer and a Wayland or X11 session with a GPU that GPUI
can drive (Vulkan). Distributions often package an older Rust;
[rustup](https://rustup.rs) installs a current one. The repo pins 1.97 in
`rust-toolchain.toml`, so with rustup the right toolchain is fetched on the
first build even if `rustup default` points at something older.

### macOS

Download `disktree-*-aarch64-macos.zip` (`x86_64-macos` for an Intel Mac)
from the [latest release](https://github.com/tobi/disktree/releases/latest),
unzip it, and drag `disktree.app` into Applications. macOS 11 or newer.

A release that was not signed and notarized is stopped by Gatekeeper: macOS
says it "is damaged and can't be opened" or "cannot be verified". The app is
fine; the browser marked the download as quarantined. Clear the mark once:

```sh
xattr -dr com.apple.quarantine /Applications/disktree.app
```

(Or open it once, then choose **Open Anyway** in System Settings › Privacy &
Security.)

Or build it, with Rust 1.97 or newer and Xcode or its Command Line Tools.
macOS does not come with Rust; install it with [rustup](https://rustup.rs).

```sh
make install     # ~/Applications/disktree.app, and ~/.local/bin/disktree
make uninstall
```

To see everything, give disktree **Full Disk Access** in System Settings ›
Privacy & Security (the panel offers a button when it is missing), then
reopen it. Without it macOS hides Mail, Messages, Safari, other apps' data
and the Trash, and disktree counts them as unreadable. Started from a
terminal, it is the terminal that needs the access. macOS also asks once
each for Desktop, Documents and Downloads.

What is different from Linux:

- **Free space** is what `df` reports. Finder's figure is larger: it counts
  purgeable space (caches and local snapshots macOS will clear on its own).
- **Cloned files** (copies APFS shares blocks between, as Finder's Duplicate
  makes) are each counted in full, so a total can exceed what deleting them
  frees.
- **Time Machine's local snapshots** are not files and do not appear; they
  are part of the gap between the scan and the disk's used space.
- **Cloud-only folders** (iCloud Drive, Dropbox and the like, evicted to the
  server) are not opened, so a scan never downloads them.

To sign and notarize a build for others, with a Developer ID certificate in
the keychain and credentials saved by `xcrun notarytool store-credentials`:

```sh
NOTARY_PROFILE=<profile> cargo xtask bundle \
  --sign "Developer ID Application: Name (TEAMID)" --notarize
```

### Windows

On Windows 10 or 11, download `disktree-*-x86_64-windows.zip`
(`aarch64-windows` on ARM) from the same release, unpack it anywhere and run
`disktree.exe`. Or build it with Rust 1.97 or newer, from
[rustup](https://rustup.rs), and the MSVC toolchain (Visual Studio Build
Tools, C++ workload):

```powershell
git clone https://github.com/tobi/disktree
cd disktree
cargo build --release    # target\release\disktree.exe
```

See [On Windows](#on-windows) for what differs there.

## Use

```sh
disktree            # scan the home directory
disktree --disk     # the whole disk it lives on
disktree ~/src

FigCraft

Interface design and prototyping: open source, collaborative and built in pure Rust.
Frames, auto layout, components and variants, vector networks, styles, variables and prototypes,
in a native app that opens instantly and works offline. Open source, and yours.


FigCraft on getartcraft.com · ArtCraft · All Crafting Apps



Ridgeline: auto layout screens built from components, with Light and Dark modes from one set of colour variables · examples/ridgeline-app.figcraft


> [!NOTE] > **ArtCraft is a community of artists from all walks of life.** Designers, illustrators, developers, > musicians, game makers — if you make things, you're one of us. **[Come say hi on Discord](https://discord.gg/artcraft).**

A look around · Made in FigCraft · Features · Agents · Under the hood · Get started · Crafting Apps · Discord


🎛️ Familiar by design

The toolbar, layers panel, Design panel, menus and shortcuts sit right where your hands expect them.

⚡ Native and fast

A Rust engine with a persistent document model: edits touch only what changed, so creating a node in a 20,000-node file takes a fraction of a millisecond. No Electron, no web view.

🔌 Offline and private

Your files are plain .figcraft archives on your own disk. No account, no telemetry, and nothing leaves your computer unless you share a file (what sharing sends where). SVG, PNG, JPG, WebP and PDF in and out; .fig files open (best effort), and so do designs exported as the public REST API file JSON, with their prototypes and variables.

🤖 Agent-ready

Every menu item, tool and drag is a command, so the same engine runs from the UI, the CLI, a JSON control channel or an MCP server.

## A look around

# Owly https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/b195ce4c-e078-49be-bc13-44a72b6dc189 AirDrop between iPhones and Linux devices whose Wi-Fi isn't Apple's Broadcom chip. See [supported hardware](#supported-hardware). ## Install
Arch/Omarchy If using Omarchy, you can install Owly together with [omdrop](https://github.com/netmojo-systems/omdrop-plugin) to get it in your bar: ```sh # Install Omdrop: omarchy plugin add https://github.com/netmojo-systems/omdrop-plugin.git # Install Owly (omdrop-owl): yay -S omdrop-owl ``` If you're just using Arch, or don't want the UI, you can just install the CLI: ```sh yay -S owly ```
NixOS ```nix inputs.owly.url = "github:t4t5/owly"; ``` ```nix imports = [ inputs.owly.nixosModules.default ]; services.owly.enable = true; services.owly.settings = { allow_untested = true; }; ```
Debian/Ubuntu Download the `.deb` from the [releases page](https://github.com/t4t5/owly/releases) and run: ```sh sudo apt install ./owly_*_amd64.deb # Debian 12, Ubuntu 22.04 and newer ```
Fedora Download the `.rpm` from the [releases page](https://github.com/t4t5/owly/releases) and run: ```sh sudo dnf install ./owly-*.x86_64.rpm # Fedora 44 and newer ```
From source Requires Rust 1.88 or newer: ```sh cargo build --release --locked -p owlyd -p owly-cli sudo packaging/install.sh owly sudo systemctl daemon-reload && sudo nmcli general reload conf ```

CCBaga

English · 简体中文

A native macOS, Linux and Windows toolkit for a cleaner workspace and an environment you can verify.

Claude identities · Browser fingerprints · System settings · Network Skill

Features · Installation · Updates · Quick start · Usage guide · Architecture · Development · Contributing

![CCBaga: native control, observable environments](docs/readme-hero.png) **Intended use:** CCBaga is intended solely for people residing or traveling abroad to manage their own Claude identities. Use that violates Anthropic's official terms of service is prohibited. CCBaga brings local maintenance and environment setup into one focused desktop workflow. Inspect Claude data before removing it, rotate your companion browser's fingerprint and restart it, align system settings with a selected region, and compare real browser readings with the machine and network exit. Two applications work together: **CCBaga-A** owns native operations; **CCBaga-B** runs an isolated Fingerprint Chromium profile. Browser measurements return to the host through a local session. Changing a setting and verifying its effect are separate steps. ## Features
Local Claude identities

Archive the current local identity, switch to a saved identity or start with an empty workspace. Choose what stays shared and what moves with each identity.		 Fingerprint & restart

Generate a fresh seed, apply the selected region's language and timezone, then restart the companion browser.		 Real environment checks

Compare browser and machine readings with the actual network exit. Passing measured checks produces a green page and a large checkmark.
Native system settings

Apply timezone, preferred language and region settings. Open desktop controls for location and permissions; see platform-specific limits.		 AI-guided network setup

Three simple steps, a coding-agent selector and a copyable Skill installation prompt. Give the AI your files and connection details; it handles the commands.		 Claude Code CLI tools

Detect the installation method and version. Uninstall or reinstall through native, npm/bun, Homebrew or WinGet workflows.
**One region selector. Four everyday actions.** Easy setup puts browser cache cleanup, fingerprint rotation, timezone/language reset and identity archiving on the same page. The sidebar keeps advanced controls in Network, Claude identities, Browser and Computer. The interface supports **English and Chinese**, with shared YAML catalogs. Switching the interface language does not change the computer or browser language. The bilingual **Usage guide** covers common actions and data boundaries. See the [full guide](docs/usage.md). ## Installation **Platforms:** macOS 12 or later on Apple Silicon; Linux x86_64 with GTK 3 and WebKitGTK 4.1; Windows 10/11 x86_64. Intel macOS and Linux ARM64 are not supported. Linux x86_64 packages include DEB, RPM and AppImage built on Ubuntu 22.04 (glibc 2.35), plus a separate package for current Arch/pacman systems. All include the companion browser. See [Linux setup](docs/linux.md) for installation and platform limits. Official versions are published exclusively by the project owner, **liseami**. Windows x86_64 uses one NSIS setup installer containing both A and B. The installer is not Authenticode

# Folkbench 中转站实测评测，与 Folkbench Switch。 [![Release](https://img.shields.io/github/v/release/Folkbench/folkbench?include_prereleases&label=release&color=7624f4&style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/Folkbench/folkbench/releases) [![Stars](https://img.shields.io/github/stars/Folkbench/folkbench?color=f5a623&logo=github&style=for-the-badge)](https://github.com/Folkbench/folkbench/stargazers) [![folkbench.com](https://img.shields.io/badge/folkbench.com-533afd?style=for-the-badge&logo=googlechrome&logoColor=white)](https://folkbench.com/?utm_source=github&utm_campaign=readme_badge) [![Telegram](https://img.shields.io/badge/Telegram-2BA2E0?logo=telegram&logoColor=white&style=for-the-badge)](https://t.me/+-h3yj4eOYmw0ZTNl) [![Group](https://img.shields.io/badge/Group-12B7F5?logo=qq&logoColor=white&style=for-the-badge)](https://qm.qq.com/q/71NzSTrPVK) [🌐 在线评测大盘](https://folkbench.com/rankings/board?utm_source=github&utm_campaign=readme) · [⚡ Switch 客户端](#folkbench-switch) · [📦 下载安装](https://github.com/Folkbench/folkbench/releases) · [🔥 热门模型](#热门模型) · [💬 交流群 (TG)](https://t.me/+-h3yj4eOYmw0ZTNl) · [💬 QQ 群](https://qm.qq.com/q/71NzSTrPVK) · [English](README.en.md) · [日本語](README.ja.md) · [Español](README.es.md)

[folkbench.com](https://folkbench.com/?utm_source=github&utm_campaign=readme) 持续测试各家 AI 中转站，公开可用率、响应耗时和价格。本仓库是配套桌面客户端 **Folkbench Switch** 的代码，用来把选好的线路写入 Claude Code、Codex 等工具的配置。 --- ## 赞助商 以下中转站支持 Folkbench 的持续评测。[成为赞助商 →](https://folkbench.com/vendor/login?utm_source=github&utm_campaign=readme)
Modelflare
Modelflare站点是由美国 Havenbyte LLC 运营，支持 GPT、Claude、Gemini、Grok 等主流模型和常用兼容协议，同时也支持 40 多种图片及视频模型。API Key 可以配置有序回退，一把 API Key 可以调用多个模型，Key 还可以设置备用分组，并且从请求日志里能看到状态、延迟、Token 和实际费用。

缓存补偿是这个站的另一个亮点：部分 OpenAI 价格优先、稳定和高级分组分别提供每日 65%、75%、85% 的缓存命中率保障，对于符合条件的api请求如果未达到缓存命中率，平台会给予对应补充。

站点目前也有首次充值解锁特惠分组的活动，单笔充值 US$20 后可解锁 GPT 特惠分组，解锁后 GPT-5.6-Sol 的价格大约是 ¥0.51（输入）/ ¥3.01（输出）/每百万 Token，并且没有使用上限限制。单笔充值 US$50 后可解锁 Claude 特惠分组。
CheapAI
CheapAI字如其名，主打一个便宜，可以重点看特惠分组，价格确实压得很低。而且还有一个很有意思的动态倍率分组。按客服的介绍，这个分组会根据实时号池情况调整倍率。资源充足的时候价格可以更低，资源紧张时则会相应调整，在价格和可用性之间实时做一个平衡。

对于追求性价比的用户可以选择它们家折扣倍率较好的特惠分组，而对于追求稳定的用户可以选择稳定分组或 Pro 分组，站点也提供官 key 分组，能够覆盖不同使用需求。
IKunCode
IKunCode对于各个编程工具接入的支持比较好，Claude Code、Codex 和 Gemini CLI 都有单独支持，售后以及咨询渠道渠道做得比较全，官网公开了客服邮箱、QQ 群和 Telegram，人工客服服务贴心，很适合新手上路。
智流 FluxLane
智流 FluxLane 的模型和线路比较多，国内外模型都有，接入方式也比较统一，直接兼容 OpenAI SDK。除了模型和线路比较全，它还把路由、用量、成本和延迟这些东西都做进了平台里，比较适合开发者和团队长期接入。对于企业和高校采购这方面是比较明显的优势，可以提供发票、合同、采购单。
